subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: When water is added to anhydrous copper(II) sulfate, what colour change is observed?
questions.explain: Anhydrous copper(II) sulfate is white and turns blue when hydrated, so it is used to test for the presence of water.

questions.q: What colour change occurs when water is added to anhydrous cobalt(II) chloride?
questions.explain: Anhydrous cobalt(II) chloride is blue and turns pink in the presence of water.

questions.q: Why is chlorine added during the treatment of the domestic water supply?
options: To kill bacteria and other microbes
questions.explain: Chlorination sterilises the water by killing harmful microbes such as bacteria.

questions.q: What is the purpose of passing water through carbon during water treatment?
questions.explain: Carbon adsorbs substances that cause unpleasant tastes and odours in the water.

questions.q: A sample of water is found to boil at 101 degrees C at standard atmospheric pressure. What does this suggest?
questions.explain: Pure water boils at exactly 100 degrees C, so a raised boiling point indicates dissolved impurities.

questions.q: Which three elements are supplied by NPK fertilisers?
questions.explain: NPK fertilisers supply the three key plant nutrients nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P) and potassium (K).

questions.q: Which of the following compounds is commonly used as a fertiliser to supply nitrogen to plants?
questions.explain: Ammonium salts and nitrates, such as ammonium nitrate, are used as fertilisers because they provide nitrogen.

questions.q: A farmer needs a fertiliser that provides nitrogen. Which formula represents a suitable ammonium salt?
questions.explain: Ammonium sulfate, (NH4)2SO4, contains the ammonium ion and so supplies nitrogen to the plant.

questions.q: Approximately what percentage of clean dry air is nitrogen?
questions.explain: Clean dry air is roughly 78% nitrogen by volume.

questions.q: Approximately what percentage of clean dry air is oxygen?
questions.explain: Clean dry air is roughly 21% oxygen by volume.

questions.q: Besides nitrogen and oxygen, which gases make up the small remaining fraction of clean dry air?
questions.explain: The remaining fraction of clean dry air is mainly the noble gas argon together with a small amount of carbon dioxide.

questions.q: How is carbon monoxide produced?
questions.explain: Carbon monoxide forms when carbon-containing fuels burn in a limited supply of oxygen (incomplete combustion).

questions.q: What is the main source and adverse effect of sulfur dioxide as an air pollutant?
options: Combustion of fossil fuels containing sulfur; causes acid rain
Digestion in animals; causes acid rain
questions.explain: Sulfur dioxide is released when sulfur-containing fossil fuels are burned and it contributes to acid rain.

questions.q: In a catalytic converter, carbon monoxide and oxides of nitrogen are converted into which less harmful gases?
questions.explain: A catalytic converter changes the toxic gases carbon monoxide and oxides of nitrogen into carbon dioxide and nitrogen.

questions.q: A region suffers from acid rain that damages buildings and lakes. Which two pollutants are mainly responsible?
options: Sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen
questions.explain: Sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen dissolve in rainwater to form the acids responsible for acid rain.

questions.q: Which two gases are the main greenhouse gases responsible for climate change?
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide and methane are the main greenhouse gases that contribute to increased global warming.

questions.q: Which of the following is a source of the greenhouse gas methane?
options: Waste gases from digestion in animals
Reaction of nitrogen and oxygen in car engines
questions.explain: Methane is released from the decomposition of vegetation and from waste gases produced by digestion in animals.

questions.q: How do greenhouse gases contribute to global warming?
options: They absorb thermal energy (infrared radiation) re-emitted from the Earth's surface
They react with oxygen to form acids
They block sunlight from reaching the Earth
questions.explain: Greenhouse gases trap thermal energy radiated from the Earth's surface, raising the temperature of the atmosphere.

questions.q: Which of the following is a strategy to reduce carbon dioxide emissions?
options: Using renewable sources of energy instead of fossil fuels
questions.explain: Switching from fossil fuels to renewable energy sources reduces the amount of carbon dioxide released into the atmosphere.

questions.q: Planting more trees helps to reduce the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere. Which process is responsible for this?
questions.explain: During photosynthesis plants take in carbon dioxide and use it, along with water and light, to make glucose and oxygen.
